briefing.headline: OpenAI o4 and DeepSeek-R2 escalate AGI timeline bets as export controls tighten

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: Frontier labs accelerate multimodal agent deployments while governments scramble to regulate dual-use capabilities. Compute demand outstrips supply, driving new sovereign AI alliances. US-China decoupling dominates strategic planning.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI released o4 with native tool-use and long-horizon planning. Anthropic's Claude 4 Opus and Meta's Llama 4 405B variant launched this week. DeepSeek-R2 matches o3 performance at 40% lower inference cost.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems. NIST issued new guidelines for agentic workflows. DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level for multi-agent and IoT deployments.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: TSMC began volume production of 1.4nm A16 process for AI accelerators. Microsoft and CoreWeave announced $4B joint hyperscale campus in Texas. Google TPU v6 pods now available via Vertex AI.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will export controls on advanced AI chips slow China's frontier progress more than US domestic scaling?
